plain_english_policy:
The Alabama Ethics Commission is made up of five members who must have high moral character, ability, and fairness. They cannot include current public officials, candidates for office, registered lobbyists (or their principals), or former commission employees.

Members are appointed by the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Senate Presiding Officer, and Speaker of the House. Their appointments require confirmation by the Senate. The first members served staggered terms from 1975; subsequent members serve five-year terms starting September 1 each year until their successors take office.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Establishes a State Ethics Commission with specific eligibility requirements for its five appointed members, outlines appointment procedures by state officers requiring Senate confirmation, and defines term lengths to ensure continuity of service.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill establishes an independent ethics commission with clear eligibility criteria for members (excluding current officials/lobbyists) and structured appointment processes to ensure balanced oversight of public conduct.
evidence_quotes: There is hereby created a State Ethics Commission composed of five members, each of whom shall be a fair, equitable citizen of this state and of high moral character and ability.

The following persons shall not be eligible to be appointed as members: (1) a public official; (2) a candidate; (3) a registered lobbyist and his or her principal; or (4) a former employee of the commission.
